items.label: Definition 5.16
items.scope: Strong convexity with positive modulus for an extended-real function with no minus-infinity values, on a finite-dimensional real inner product space. The effective domain is convex and closed-interval convex combinations satisfy the quadratic deficit inequality.

items.label: Theorem 5.17
items.scope: Equivalence between strong convexity and convexity of f minus one half of the modulus times the squared norm, retaining the complete extended-real domain and allowing an empty effective domain.

books.title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

items.label: Definition 10.7
items.scope: The strong-convexity specialization for proper extended-real functions on an arbitrary real Hilbert space, using strictly interior convex weights.

items.label: Proposition 10.8
items.scope: Both directions of the equivalence between positive-modulus strong convexity and convexity after subtracting the half-modulus squared-norm term.

items.label: Definition 2.1.3, equation (2.1.20)
items.scope: Positive-modulus strong convexity expressed by a first-order lower bound on a convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space. The norm is arbitrary and the derivative is paired with a direction.

items.label: Theorem 2.1.9
items.scope: Equivalence of the first-order lower bound with strong monotonicity of the derivative and the closed-interval quadratic Jensen inequality. The domain need not be open, full-dimensional, or nonempty; the differentiability convention is independently reviewed.

items.label: Lemma 5.20
items.scope: An extended-real sigma-strongly convex function plus a convex function is sigma-strongly convex for sigma > 0.

items.label: Example 5.21
items.scope: For a nonempty convex subset C of a Euclidean space, one half of the squared norm plus the indicator of C is 1-strongly convex.

items.label: Lemma 2.1.6
items.scope: For nonnegative alpha and beta, alpha f1 + beta f2 has strong-convexity parameter alpha mu1 + beta mu2 on Q1 intersect Q2.

items.label: Theorem 2.1.8
items.scope: If f belongs to S_mu^1 on the whole finite-dimensional space and its gradient vanishes at x_star, f(x) >= f(x_star) + (mu/2) norm(x-x_star)^2 for every x.

books.title: Convex Analysis and Monotone Operator Theory in Hilbert Spaces

items.label: Example 22.4(iv)
items.scope: For a proper convex extended-real function on a real Hilbert space, beta-strong convexity with beta > 0 implies beta-strong monotonicity of the subdifferential.

items.label: Proposition 23.13
items.scope: A monotone operator A is beta-strongly monotone iff its resolvent is (beta+1)-cocoercive; consequently the resolvent is 1/(beta+1)-Lipschitz.
